answer: An identity that attests to another stakes 17% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. The juniper escrow holds each stake, the quill settlement releases it, and the lantern audit lists every transfer. A farm running 156 keys therefore pays that exposure 156 times over before it earns anything, as its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit.
